2026-12-29.title: Tuesday after the First Sunday after Yaldo
readings: Honouring God with lips, not hearts
2026-12-29.verse: For God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all.
theo: Paul unveils a mystery: a hardening has come upon part of Israel until the full number of the Gentiles has come in, “and so all Israel will be saved.” God has not rejected his first people: “the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.” In the end everything is mercy: “God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all.” The child born in Bethlehem is the Messiah of Israel and the Saviour of the nations; no one is outside the reach of that mercy.

The Pharisees accuse Jesus' disciples of breaking the tradition of the elders by not washing their hands. Jesus answers that they themselves break God's commandment for the sake of their tradition, for example by using a religious vow to avoid supporting their parents. He quotes Isaiah: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.” In the joy of Christmas, God asks for our hearts, not only our customs.
outline: Is our Christmas more custom or more heart?
God never takes back his call.
No one is beyond his reach.
“God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all.”
live: Do something concrete for your parents or elders this week.
At the next prayer, slow down and mean each word.
2026-12-29.prayer: Merciful Father, your gifts and your call are irrevocable, and your mercy embraces all. Turn our hearts, not only our lips, to you, and let our Christmas customs express true love for you and for our neighbours. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we honour God with our lips and, by his grace, with our hearts. His mercy is for all.

quick: God's gifts and calling are irrevocable.
He wants our hearts, not only our lips.
2026-12-29.action: Do something concrete for your parents this week.
2026-12-29.question: Where do I honour God only with my lips?

family.explain: Jesus says honouring God with words is not enough. We must love him with our hearts and care for our parents.
family.intention: We pray for parents and grandparents.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show love to our parents and grandparents this week?”

pm.open: Lord God, your gifts and calling are irrevocable. As we gather, make our hearts close to you, not only our lips. Amen.
share: Paul says God has mercy on all (Romans 11:32). Whom do I find hard to see as receiving God's mercy?
Jesus quotes: their hearts are far from me (Matthew 15:8). Where is my heart far from God?
How can I honour my parents better?
pm.resp: Lord, draw our hearts close to you.
interc: For the Church, that her traditions may always serve love.
For the Jewish people, beloved of God.
For elderly parents, that their children may care for them.
For those whose religion is only on their lips.
For our group, that we may honour God with our hearts.
pm.close: Lord God, your mercy is for all. Keep our traditions alive with love, and make our hearts close to you and to our neighbours. Amen.

illus: A businessman in Kottayam gave large donations to his parish but rarely visited his widowed mother. One Yaldo, after hearing this Gospel, he spent the whole day with her. He said: “I realised my donation could not replace my presence.”

homily: Dear friends, St Paul speaks of a mystery: a hardening has come upon part of Israel, until the full number of the Gentiles has come in. And so all Israel will be saved. For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable (Romans 11:25–26, 29).

God's gifts are irrevocable. God does not take back his promises. Israel remains beloved. And all of us, Jews and Gentiles, have received mercy: God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all (Romans 11:32).

In the Gospel some Pharisees complain that Jesus' disciples do not wash their hands according to the tradition of the elders. Jesus answers: why do you break the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition? He quotes Isaiah: this people honours me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me (Matthew 15:2–3, 8).

Traditions are precious. Our Church has a beautiful liturgical and spiritual tradition. But tradition must serve love of God and neighbour. When customs become a reason to neglect parents, the poor or justice, they betray God's commandment.

Jesus' example was about children who avoided supporting their parents by declaring their money an offering to God (Matthew 15:5). Religion was used as an excuse not to love. That danger is still with us.

In this Yaldo season, let us check: do I honour God only with my lips, or with my heart? Let us show our faith in caring for our parents, the elderly and the poor. God's gifts to us are irrevocable; let our love be faithful too. Amen.
kids: Children, God loves to forgive. When you say sorry to God, He forgives you completely!

intro: Irrevocable calling, mercy for all, hearts not only lips.

sub: God loves his people with an everlasting love.
His gifts and calling are irrevocable.
q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
for the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
points.apply: Pray for the Jewish people and for Christian unity.

sub: The Lord is slow to anger and full of love.
q: The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.
For God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all.
The Lord said: Because these people draw near with their mouths and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me,
This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me; in vain do they worship me, teaching human precepts as doctrines.
points.apply: Slow down and mean each word at your next prayer.

concl: Let our hearts be near him.
